newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE - BARCELONA PEN PIX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE - BARCELONA PEN PIX.

text.p: Pen pictures of the players most likely to be in the Barcelona squad against Real Betis in the Spanish Cup final on Saturday:

Vitor Baia. Goalkeeper. Age 27. The Portuguese international keeper signed from Porto last summer for $6.34 million. Rated as one of the best keepers in the world but his reputation has suffered recently with some poor preformances. Let in 43 goals during the 1996-97 league season.

Carlos Busquets. Goalkeeper. 29. Former Barcelona number one but displaced by the arrival of Baia. Has not impressed in on the few chances he has had and remains the second string keeper despite Baia's recent problems.

Albert Ferrer. Defender, 27. Right-sided defender who won a gold medal with the 1992 Spanish Olympic team. Struggled to secure a regular first team place under coach Bobby Robson but did well in the the Cup Winners Cup final.

Abdelardo Fernandez. Defender. 27. An experienced Spanish international and solid central defender. Speculation about whether he will move at the end of the season despite being among the fans' favourite players.
Laurent Blanc. Defender. 31. French international but has had to compete with Abdelardo for playing time due to Barcelona's wealth of defenders. One of Johan Cruyff's last signings.

Fernando Couto. Defender. 27. One of three Portugese internationals in the Barcelona squad. Skillful on the ground and likes to attack. Headed a controversially disallowed goal in the Cup Winners Cup final.
Sergi Barjuan. Defender. 25. Another Spanish international and one of the few Barcelona players with a guarenteed place on the team sheet. One of the quickest men in the Spanish first division.
Miguel Angel Nadal. Defender/midfielder. 30. Surprisingly skillfull for a big man and a danger at set pieces. Robson has resisted several big offers for him to ensure he stayed at Barcelona.
Gheorge Popescu. Defender/midfielder. 29. Often the captain. The Romanian international has proved himself to be a strong man in the centre of the field and good distributor of the ball.

Luis Enrique Martinez. Midfielder. 27. Energetic utility player with a high work rate who Robson recently said was the first to go on the team sheet every match. Won over the fans after moving from Real Madrid in 1996 and a regular Spanish international. 17 league goals last season, second best for Barcelona behind Ronaldo.

Josep Guardiola. Midfielder. 26. Shares the captain's armband with Popescu. Found a new lease of life under Robson after being regularly dropped during Cruyff's last year at the club. Free kick specialist.

Ivan de la Pena. Midfielder. 21. Shaven-haired darling of the Camp Nou crowd. Out of favour at the start of the season but is now less inconsistant and commands a regular place. Had an outstanding Cup Winners Cup final.
Guilermo Amor. Midfielder. 29. Played for Spain during Euro '96 but has spent much of this season on the bench.
Roger Garcia. 20. Midfielder. Born locally and a product of the Barcelona junior teams. A regular under Cruyff but has found himself displaced by the arrival of the foreign stars at Camp Nou.

Oscar Garcia. Midfielder. 24. Back up midfielder but has been occasionally starting games in recent months. Another local boy who has worked his way through the Barcelona junior teams. Luis Figo. Striker. 24. Portugese international winger who is at home on either side of the pitch. One of the stars of the Cup Winners Cup final triumph.

Ronaldo. Striker. 20. The Brazilain international was rated the best player in the world last year in a FIFA poll of international managers. Broke the long-standing Barcelona single-season scoring record with 34 league goals. Last week signed for Italian club Internazionale for a world record four billion pesetas ($27.5 million) but FIFA have suggested that the move may contravene international transfer regulations and Barcelona president Josep Luis Nunez has suggested that Ronaldo could stuill turn out for them on Saturday.
Juan Pizzi. Striker. 29. A naturalised Argentinian who has been in the shadow of Ronaldo. Reputation for squandering good goal opportunities.
Hristo Stoichkov. Striker. 31. Voletile Bulgarian international who has been mainly used as a backup striker in recent months.

Emmanuel Ammunike. Striker. 26. Robson's only mid-season signing. The Nigerian international's form has slumped since arriving at Barcelona from Sporting Lisbon and recently publically criticised Robson over being frequently used as a substitute.
Angel Manuel Cuellar. Striker. 24. Backup striker who has not got many minutes on the field this season. Could be on the bench on Saturday.
